column2: we are not correctly DMA unmapping TX buffers for

column1: fragments.
Indeed
column2: the mvpp2_txq_inc_put() function only stores in the

column1: txq_cpu->tx_buffs[] array the physical address of the buffer to be
DMA-unmapped when skb != NULL. In addition
skb_headlen(skb) to get the size to be unmapped. Both of this works fine
for TX descriptors that are associated directly to a SKB
ones that are used for fragments
column2: with a NULL pointer as skb:

column1: - We have a NULL physical address when calling DMA unmap
- skb_headlen(skb) crashes because skb is NULL
This causes random crashes when fragments are used.
To solve this problem
- Store the physical address of the buffer to be unmapped
unconditionally
column2: regardless of whether it is tied to a SKB or not.

column1: - Store the length of the buffer to be unmapped
field.
Instead of adding a third array to store the length of the buffer to be
unmapped
column2: and as suggested by David Miller

column1: tx_buffs[] and tx_skb[] arrays of 'struct mvpp2_txq_pcpu' into a
separate structure 'mvpp2_txq_pcpu_buf'
added. Therefore
column2: instead of having three arrays to allocate/free

column1: have a single one
impact on the CPU cache.
